label: Cartoony simulator / pet-sim / clicker
provenance: Screenshots of shipped Roblox games and published UI kits, supplied by the owner as the standard to hit. No image is stored; each row records where it was seen and what it demonstrates.

references.source: shipped simulator, in-game Store with Limited / Money / Passes tabs
demonstrates: banner title 'Store!' sits ABOVE the panel body and overhangs it, with a small icon tucked against the word
tab row directly under the banner: pill buttons, the active one filled, inactive ones outlined
gamepass tiles are a 4-across grid of square cards, each with icon, name, and either a price pill or the word OWNED
owned state replaces the price entirely rather than greying the button — the card still reads as a card
bottom action row is four equal chunky buttons in a single colour (PLAY / BACK / SETTINGS / QUIT)
currency readouts run along the very top as separate pills, each with its own icon

references.source: published Roblox UI kit sheet — Pets, Shop, Settings, Codes, Trade panels plus a side rail
demonstrates: one visual language across every panel: same corner radius, same stroke, same header treatment
header is a narrower bar centred on top of the panel, reading as a plaque rather than a title bar
the side rail is a vertical stack of square icon buttons, each labelled underneath in small text
inner content areas are a LIGHTER tint of the panel colour, never white, and inset with visible padding
item slots are empty rounded squares in that lighter tint — the grid reads even with no content
destructive and confirming actions are colour-coded (green Accept, red Cancel) and sit at the top of the trade panel, not the bottom

references.source: shipped pet simulator, SHOP modal over a grey-box world
demonstrates: modal is a tall near-white sheet with a red header bar and a red circular X overhanging the top-right corner
featured offer is a full-width band at the top with its own background tint, larger art and a price pill
below it, a 3-across row of small square offers, then full-width currency rows
every price is a pill containing a currency icon then the number, never bare text
section bands alternate background tint so the list reads as groups without drawing separator lines
left edge of the screen carries a vertical icon rail; bottom centre carries the level bar and cash readout

references.source: published UI kit thumbnail — Inventory with category rail, item grid and detail pane
demonstrates: three-column layout: narrow category list, wide item grid, narrow detail pane
category buttons are stacked pills, the selected one a different hue
item grid is 4-across rounded squares with the name on a small bar across the top of each tile
detail pane shows the item large, then a description block, then a single green Equip button at the bottom
the whole assembly sits on one rounded panel with a single outer stroke, not three separate windows
close is a red circle at the top-right of the OUTER panel, overhanging it

references.source: shipped obby/simulator hybrid, prize wheel with a bottom-left button rail
demonstrates: the wheel is segmented in saturated primaries with white dividing lines and a white pointer
each segment carries an icon and a short all-caps label, rotated to the segment
the launcher rail is circular icon buttons with the label directly beneath in small bold text
circular buttons get the same thick dark stroke as rectangular panels — the stroke is the constant, not the shape

references.source: shipped simulator, Codes modal over a beach scene
demonstrates: small single-purpose modal: banner title, one line of instruction, one text field, one confirm button
the text field is white with a dark stroke and rounded ends, with placeholder text in grey
the confirm button is green, chunky, and noticeably smaller than the field above it
modal width is roughly a third of the screen — a one-field dialog does not become a full sheet

references.source: published store panel template, blue with Limited / Gamepass / Money tabs
demonstrates: clearest reading of the construction: panel stroke is very thick and near-black, corner radius is large
the title plaque is a separate rounded bar overlapping the panel's top edge, with its own stroke
content area is split into two equal rounded sub-panels with a diagonal stripe texture at low contrast
the red X is a circle with the same near-black stroke, sitting proud of the top-right corner
tab pills sit on the panel body just below the plaque, not inside the content area
seven-day strip of equal tiles, each with the day label on top, the reward icon centred, the amount beneath
the claimable day is highlighted with a brighter tile and a green Claim! button directly under it
the banner title is set at a slight angle and overhangs the left edge — the angle is deliberate and is part of the style
a single wide secondary button ('Unlock All Reward') sits under the strip in a quieter colour

references.source: shipped simulator, DIAMONDS shop with a striped awning header
demonstrates: header is an awning/canopy graphic rather than a flat bar — the plaque can be illustrative
the best-value offer is a wide band with a BEST tag, larger art and a bonus line in a contrasting colour
remaining offers are a 2x2 grid of equal tiles, one tagged HOT
the panel body is a warm parchment tint while the surrounding chrome stays saturated — the sheet is allowed to be a different family from the frame
left and right screen edges carry vertical icon rails, mirrored

references.source: published kit — Stats, Rebirth, Pets, Gem Shop, Trading, Season panels on one sheet
demonstrates: a complete game's panels share one plaque style, one stroke weight and one radius across nine different panels
Stats is a list of label/value rows, each row its own rounded strip with an icon at the left
Rebirth rows pair a progress bar with a cost pill and a button on the same row
Season shows a quest list with a vertical progress track down the right edge
the bottom-left launcher rail is circular buttons, matching the spin-wheel reference — this rail is a convention, not one game's choice

rules.note: Distilled from the references above. Units are Roblox UI units: px for stroke and radius, unitless for scale. Values are read proportionally from screenshots, not sampled, and are stated as approximations.

panelStroke.why: every reference outlines every panel, card and button in the same near-black; it is the single most identifying feature and the simulator theme shipped with stroke 3 applied inconsistently

cornerRadius.why: large and consistent; a small radius immediately reads as a developer tool

header.why: in eight of ten references the title is a separate rounded bar overlapping the panel's top edge, not text inside the panel

buttonBevel.why: chunky buttons read as pressable because the top half is lighter and a darker band sits along the bottom

textStroke.why: white text over saturated fills is illegible without it, and every reference uses it

closeButton.why: a red circle proud of the corner in six references; a square X inside the header reads as a dialog, not a game

contentTint.rule: inner areas are a lighter tint of the panel, or a near-white sheet — never the panel colour itself
contentTint.why: flat panels lose their grid; every reference separates frame from content

priceDisplay.rule: icon then number inside a pill

ownedState.rule: replace the price pill with the word OWNED
ownedState.never: disable the button and leave the price
ownedState.why: seen in the gamepass grid; keeps the card readable

launcherRail.why: appears in three independent references, so it is a convention rather than one game's choice

grid.why: four-across square tiles in five references; the shipped kit used tall 240px cards which is why it reads as a list rather than a shop

gapsAgainstShippedTheme: CLOSED: no thick dark stroke on cards or buttons — outline() defaults to theme.outline at >=2px, button() strokes at >=3px
CLOSED: no stroke on any text — strokeText(), thickness SCALED to glyph size after a flat 2px rendered 16px labels as black blobs
CLOSED: flat buttons — a UIGradient bevel lightens the top 55% and darkens the bottom edge to 0.82
CLOSED: no plaque header — the title is now a rounded accent-coloured bar with its own stroke, overhanging the panel's top edge
CLOSED: close was a rounded rect labelled Close — now a red circle centred on the top-right corner, proud of the panel
OPEN: prices render as bare text ('75 coins') rather than an icon-then-number pill
OPEN: item icons are flat diamonds rather than the gradient tiles every reference uses
OPEN: tiles are 2-across and tall; the references pack 4-across squares

renderedAndCompared.how: AppleUI installed into a Studio place and played; simulator theme; compared against the references in this file by looking at the result
renderedAndCompared.note: The text-stroke defect was invisible in the source and obvious on screen. That is the argument for this loop existing.
